details: Assigning a label to an entire graph — e.g. classifying molecules by activity — using graph neural networks that pool node information into a graph-level representation.

explainer.lead: Graph classification gives one label to an entire network of connected things, rather than labeling each thing separately. It matters when the overall pattern of connections—such as the structure of a molecule—determines the answer.

tiers.eli5: Imagine looking at a whole team and deciding whether it is a football team or a basketball team, instead of labeling every player. Graph classification does something similar with connected dots: it considers the whole pattern and gives it one label. For example, it can look at a molecule's structure and predict whether that molecule is active.
tiers.practitioner: Train on graphs that each have a graph-level label, using a graph neural network to produce node representations and a pooling step to combine them into one graph representation. A classifier then predicts the label. A key pitfall is that pooling can discard structural details needed to distinguish graphs, so the pooling choice deserves testing.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a graph G and its label y, graph classification learns a function f(G) that predicts y. A graph neural network computes node representations, pooling maps them to a graph-level representation h_G, and a classifier maps h_G to the predicted label. Pooling creates a fixed graph-level summary but can lose information present in the node representations.

explainer.example: Represent a molecule as a graph, pool the information learned for its nodes into one molecular representation, and classify the molecule as active or inactive.

usedIn.name: Molecular activity prediction
usedIn.detail: Classifying a molecule's graph by whether it shows a particular activity.

usedIn.name: Graph neural networks
usedIn.detail: Pooling node information into a representation used for graph-level prediction.

explainer.intuition: A graph can have a meaningful property that belongs to the whole structure, not to any single node. Graph classification summarizes the nodes and their connections so the entire graph can receive one label.
howItWorks: Provide a graph with nodes and connections.
Use a graph neural network to build node representations.
Pool the node information into one graph-level representation.
Pass that representation to a classifier.
Output a single label for the whole graph.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turns an entire relational structure into a prediction, allowing graph neural networks to handle tasks whose labels describe whole graphs. Molecular activity classification is one example.
misconceptions: It is not node classification: the output labels the whole graph, not individual nodes.
Pooling is not the final classification: it creates the representation that the classifier uses.
One graph produces one graph-level label, even when it contains many nodes.
